records-needed-to-decide-the-proposal.text: Records needed to decide the proposal.
As a model reviewer, I want to see exactly what an identity or evidence record contains and which assertions are still hypothetical.

configuration-and-application-controls.text: The bound root Config contains the four policy pins plus root, minimum tip, processing/reclaim windows, registry identity, registration cost and booking width. The four-field proposal is not adopted by this plan. The investigation must account for each field and preserve every required economic obligation.

The bound application has a registry-parameterized App and protected Control fields. Changing that dependency requires a recorded comparison of controller update, genuine-token release and pending-custody behavior. This table specifies no replacement wire datum.

frozen-candidate-records.text: These records are hypotheses under the identity, role and hash questions, constrained by the complete-identity ruling. They define no ledger laws or wire migration.

The minimal transaction view must later bind to accepted ledger/history vocabulary, as impact.md records. It cannot establish ledger validity, lineage, custody, supply or real hash collision freedom. Economic configuration and the termination custody ruling belong to subsequent stages.

frozen-application-held-records.text: The records below belong only to NoPin.Held. They are explicitly hypothetical. They specify no wire layout, policy implementation or cancellation ruling. The public application address family is distinct from logical custody classification.

Authentication, supply and availability statements name the explicit root projection and its reachability premises. Root abstract tags and candidate shared-policy assets require a named correspondence; new identities use the existing parameterized NoPin hash/codec, never the root FNV stand-ins. Calling the unchanged root admission reads its accepted tag definition and does not adopt that stand-in as a new cryptographic construction.
